rules.statement: Don't write OAuth 2.0 or OpenID Connect wire names (parameter names, error codes, grant types, response types, discovery metadata members, media types, well-known paths) as string literals or redeclare them in a local constants class; reference the single shared protocol-vocabulary constant.
rules.why: A name repeated as a literal or a private constant has several copies that drift apart (issue #353); each wire name should exist once.
rules.check: Look for string literals like "client_id", "invalid_grant", "authorization_code", "application/x-www-form-urlencoded", "jwks_uri" or new constant classes holding such names in client, BFF or server code, where the shared protocol vocabulary already defines them.

rules.statement: Put a new name that crosses the wire in the dependency-free protocol-vocabulary class, and put a name only the server uses (endpoint names, internal `$`-prefixed parameters, persisted grant types, policy codes) in the server's own constants class.
rules.why: Relying parties can only reach the dependency-free package, so wire names placed in the server's constants force duplication, and server-only names placed in the protocol package pollute the shared vocabulary.
rules.check: For each added constant, check whether it appears on the wire; a wire name added to the server constants class, or a server-only or internal name added to the protocol vocabulary, is misplaced.

rules.statement: Keep the protocol-vocabulary abstractions package a leaf with no project, package or framework references; when a name in it seems to need a reference, move that name somewhere else.
rules.why: Relying parties must be able to reference the vocabulary without pulling in persistence, settings, ASP.NET Core or other server abstractions.
rules.check: Look for added ProjectReference, PackageReference or FrameworkReference entries in the protocol abstractions project file.

rules.statement: Don't let relying-party packages (protocol client, backend-for-frontend) reference OpenID Provider packages; they get protocol names only from the dependency-free vocabulary package.
rules.why: The design forbids relying parties from depending on the OP's packages.
rules.check: Look for project or package references from client or BFF projects to OP packages, or usings of OP-only namespaces in them.

rules.statement: Take JWT and JOSE claim names from `JoseClaimNames` and don't redefine them in the OAuth/OIDC protocol vocabulary; the protocol vocabulary keeps only protocol-specific values such as event names.
rules.why: A claim name is JOSE vocabulary, and duplicating it in the protocol constants would create a second copy (e.g. the back-channel logout `events` claim is `JoseClaimNames.Payload.Events`, RFC 8417).
rules.check: Look for claim-name constants or literals ("sub", "events", "iss", ...) added to the protocol vocabulary or used directly instead of `JoseClaimNames`.

rules.statement: Define server endpoint names and discoverable setting names from the matching protocol discovery-metadata constant rather than a separate literal, but don't alias a different concept that only shares the spelling.
rules.why: Each discovery name should have one copy, while a different concept (such as a client-registration `jwks_uri` setting) aliased to it would couple unrelated meanings.
rules.check: Look for server constants that redeclare a discovery metadata name as a literal, and for aliases that tie a same-spelled but semantically different setting to the metadata constant.

rules.statement: Don't treat protocol vocabulary constants (grant types, client-authentication methods, response types and the like) as a closed set; code must still accept values registered by consumers or sibling packages.
rules.why: The constants name well-known members of open vocabularies and close no vocabulary.
rules.check: Look for validation, switches or enums that reject any value not among the well-known constants where the vocabulary is open.
